fields.description: What kind of entry this is, in a closed vocabulary this app owns rather than a society's. It is display only: the task's own status is the state machine, and nothing in the code branches on this value. It exists so a thread reads as a conversation instead of a column of undifferentiated notes.
fields.label: Entry
fields.options:
assigned
accepted
question
answer
progress requested
progress
submitted
completed
returned
cancelled

fields.description: Who wrote it. The login, taken from the session at the moment the entry was written and never passed in by a caller, so a thread cannot be made to say somebody said something they did not.
fields.label: Author

fields.description: When it was written. Stamped by the service, not by the form, so the order of a conversation is the order it happened in.
fields.label: Posted On

fields.description: What was said, in the author's own words. Plain text, and rendered as a string wherever it is shown, for the same reason an announcement body is plain: writing on a record somebody else will open is not permission to run markup in their browser.
fields.label: Note

fields.description: A photograph attached to this entry, most usefully a volunteer's evidence that the work was done. One image per entry rather than a gallery on the task: proof belongs to the moment it was offered, and a second photograph is a second entry with its own note and its own time.
fields.label: Attachment
